name: Aphanostephus

project_scope.installer_dependency: Both species already have canonical learner cards in the current manifest; do not reinstall either. A. riddellii has three physically present images, A. skirrhobasis has two; diagnostic photography belongs to the photo lane.
project_scope.range_note: Preserve A. skirrhobasis UNRESOLVED target-zone status.
project_scope.photo_inventory_checked: 2026-10-18: five individual JPEG paths re-fetched from main, three for A. riddellii and two for A. skirrhobasis. Physical presence does not certify identity, part visibility, or diagnostic adequacy.

look_here_first: Start with annual versus perennial habit; turn a head over to examine overlapping pale-margined phyllaries; use mature disc florets and magnified cypsela hairs for a confident species split.
shared_genus_traits: Small radiate Asteraceae heads with pale ray florets and yellow disc florets; color alone does not identify the genus.
Overlapping involucral phyllaries and a conical receptacle; mature fruit morphology is important for separating similar small daisies.
Narrow to dissected leaves and small solitary radiate heads are useful recognition cues, but variable and not sufficient to distinguish A. riddellii from A. skirrhobasis.

shared_structure_examples.plain: One daisy-like head contains many tiny ray and disc flowers.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: same-scale front and side flower-head macro

shared_structure_examples.plain: Several overlapping rows of bracts wrap the underside of each head; inspect their pale margins.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: underside of mature head with scale

shared_structure_examples.plain: The base of a mature central floret may be bulbously swollen in A. skirrhobasis.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: dissected mature disc floret under magnification

shared_structure_examples.plain: Tiny hairs on the dry one-seeded fruit bend in different patterns between species.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: matched microscope photographs of mature fruits

species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Examine roots and several mature plants; do not infer from a cropped flower photo.
Dissect fully mature disc florets under magnification; immature heads unreliable.

species_comparison_matrix.skirrhobasis: Curved or coiled predominantly in one direction
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Matched magnified mature fruits; targeted regional-key verification pending.
Overlapping character; not a species separator.

species_comparison_matrix.skirrhobasis: Taprooted annual; no persistent perennial crown expected
species_comparison_matrix.riddellii: Perennial; inspect persistent base or repeated growth
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Photograph a whole mature plant with root/crown, not a clipped shoot; distinguish true perennial base from a large annual.

species_comparison_matrix.skirrhobasis: Low, branching, often decumbent to ascending, hairy
species_comparison_matrix.riddellii: Variable perennial branching; posture may overlap with skirrhobasis
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Include whole plant and habitat; use only as supporting context, never a species-level proof.

species_comparison_matrix.skirrhobasis: Basal and alternate cauline leaves, oblanceolate to narrow; lower leaves can be lobed or toothed
species_comparison_matrix.riddellii: Narrow or finely divided leaves reported in current learner card; variation needs matched study
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Compare basal and mid-stem leaves with ruler; leaf divisions alone cannot settle the pair.

species_comparison_matrix.skirrhobasis: Overlapping rows, pale scarious margins; species-level phyllary-tip distinction not yet verified
species_comparison_matrix.riddellii: Overlapping pale-margined phyllaries; species-level tip distinction not yet verified
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Photograph underside and side of mature head at matched scale; do not invent a nonoverlapping phyllary-tip key.

species_comparison_matrix.skirrhobasis: Angular or strongly ribbed cypsela; short crown/scales reported in canonical species record
species_comparison_matrix.riddellii: Mature cypsela and pappus require source-backed comparison
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Collect mature fruit and image face, ribs, pappus and hair tips with calibrated magnification; do not infer from rays.

look_here_first: Identify a composite head and check the underside phyllaries.
Record whole-plant life cycle and basal versus stem leaves.
Dissect mature disc florets and fruits when the species matters.
Leave uncertain plants at Aphanostephus until mature diagnostic material is available.
overlap_cautions: Both species have similar pale rays and yellow centers.
A. pilosus and small Erigeron may resemble these plants; compare receptacle, phyllaries, cypsela ribs and pappus rather than flower color.
The fruit-hair distinction needs an authoritative key and actual magnified specimen verification before any arrows.

comparison_cards.look_here_first: Whole plant and root first, mature disc florets and cypsela hairs second.

comparison_cards.title: What a flower-only photo cannot tell you
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Both have small pale-rayed heads. Mark species unresolved when only flower color or one head is visible.

diagnostic_review_handoffs: Taxonomy lane: independently verify regional-key fruit-hair and mature disc-corolla-base distinctions, and any infraspecific concept before annotation; preserve existing range and taxon statuses.

Diagnostic Photo lane: five installed portraits are available as references but do not fulfill specialist anatomy roles; prioritize roots, phyllaries, disc-corolla bases and fruit hairs with ruler/magnification and individually cleared rights.
Approved Taxa Installer lane: both species are already in the canonical manifest; no new card installation is requested.

anatomy_lessons.title: Recognize the head, then flip it
anatomy_lessons.look_here_first: Find one small radiate daisy head, then photograph the side and underside where the phyllaries overlap.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Ray color and yellow disc are shared; involucre structure helps test the genus, but does not alone split these two species.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: matched front, side and underside views with millimeter scale

anatomy_lessons.title: Follow the stem to the root
anatomy_lessons.look_here_first: Trace one intact flowering stem down to its base; compare basal and stem leaves.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: The annual A. skirrhobasis versus perennial A. riddellii distinction is strongest on intact plants; a clipped flowering sprig cannot prove duration.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: matched whole plants, basal stems and roots/crowns with ruler

anatomy_lessons.title: Dissect a mature central flower
anatomy_lessons.look_here_first: Remove a mature central disc floret and inspect the base under a dissecting microscope.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: A bulbously swollen disc-corolla base is reported for A. skirrhobasis; the comparison with A. riddellii needs actual matched mature specimens.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: paired dissected mature disc-floret bases at matching magnification

anatomy_lessons.title: Examine the fruit hairs
anatomy_lessons.look_here_first: Place fully mature dry fruits flat under a microscope and focus on the tiny hair tips.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Reported one-directional curled hairs in A. skirrhobasis versus opposing hooked hairs in A. riddellii are a potential high-value separator; independently confirm the regional key before labeling arrows.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: paired mature cypsela faces, hair tips and pappus at calibrated magnification
